question: If at same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is ₹40 and compound interest is ₹65, then what is the principal (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For 2 years, Rate (R%) = [200 × (CI − SI)] ÷ SI

⇒ R = [200 × (65 − 40)] ÷ 40 = (200 × 25) ÷ 40 = 5000 ÷ 40 = 125%

Now, Principal (P) = (SI × 100) ÷ (R × T)

⇒ P = (40 × 100) ÷ (125 × 2) = 4000 ÷ 250 = 16

**∴ The correct answer is ₹16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) for 2 years = ₹40

Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years = ₹65

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 P = ?
 
 
 1st Yr: ₹20
 
 
 2nd Yr: ₹20
 
 
 Diff: ₹25
 
 Rate (R%)
 
 Total SI = ₹40 | Total CI = ₹20 + ₹20 + ₹25 = ₹65

**Calculations:**

⇒ Simple Interest remains the same for every year. Thus, SI for 1 year = ₹40 ÷ 2 = ₹20.

⇒ Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = ₹65 − ₹40 = ₹25.

⇒ In compound interest, this extra ₹25 in the 2nd year is the interest earned on the 1st year's simple interest (₹20).

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (Interest on Interest ÷ SI for 1 year) × 100

⇒ R = (25 ÷ 20) × 100 = 125%

⇒ We know that SI for 1 year = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 20 = (P × 125 × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ 20 = P × 1.25

⇒ P = 20 ÷ 1.25 = 16

**∴ The correct answer is ₹16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

SI vs CI Difference for 2 Years

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for 2 years is given by the formula D = P × (R ÷ 100)².

SI vs CI Difference for 3 Years

For 3 years, the difference formula becomes D = P × (R ÷ 100)² × (3 + R ÷ 100).

Relation between SI and CI for 2 Years

If the principal and rate are the same, CI for 2 years can be directly related to SI using: CI = SI × (1 + R ÷ 200).
